Introduction, Scope and Product Description** Establishment: Orange District Fruit Co-operative Ltd Address: 72 Station Road, Victoria Commodity: Chickpeas (Desi, Kabuli), Red Lentils Scope: Receival, drying, cleaning, sizing, colour sorting and packing of chickpeas and lentils for export. Registered area RE-QLD-2891, Millmerran facility. Intended use: Chickpeas for retail and food service. Red lentils for retail soup/curry packs. Destinations: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Middle East. **2. HACCP Team** Manager 72 (Quality Lead) Operator 72A Operator 72B **3. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)** Hygiene and Sanitation Program (DDPE-HSP-001): • Pre-season: full clean-down of receival pit, conveyors, pre-cleaner, gravity table, colour sorter and packing lines. • During season: colour sorter air nozzles cleaned daily; packing tables sanitised between shifts. • Personnel: handwash on entry; no food in processing area; dust masks and gloves provided. • Records: Cleaning Register (DDPE-CLN-01) signed after each event. [DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED] Waste management procedures for Orange District Fruit Co-operative Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented. **7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)** Pest Control Program (DDPE-PCP-001): • Rodents: 14 perimeter bait stations; monthly inspection; licensed contractor quarterly. • Insects: pitfall traps in sealed shed; phosphine fumigation when insects detected. • Bird exclusion: netting at loading bay; doors kept closed. • Records: Pest Control Log (DDPE-PC-01) monthly. **8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)** [DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]

This HACCP plan does not include a documented traceability system linking receival, processing, packing and dispatch. Specifically absent: • No lot coding system for receival batches. • No documented one-step-back / one-step-forward traceability procedure. • No dispatch register linking packed bags to container and destination. • No recall procedure or trace exercise schedule. ACTION REQUIRED: Implement a Traceability System covering: (a) Unique lot codes at receival; (b) Processing batch records; (c) Packing lot codes on bags; (d) Dispatch register; (e) Annual trace exercise; (f) Recall activation protocol; (g) Record retention minimum 2 years. **9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)** [DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan. Failed Goods Procedure (DDPE-FGP-001): • Mycotoxin exceedance: lot placed on HOLD; re-test; if confirmed — downgrade to feed or destroy. • Pesticide MRL failure: quarantine; reject export; notify grower; DAFF notified. • Foreign material detection: stop line; remove contaminant; inspect batch; re-run. • Non-conformance records maintained in DDPE-NCR register. **10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)** [DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED] No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Orange District Fruit Co-operative Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch. **11. Verification and Record Keeping** Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.

External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic). CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years. HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance. **12. OVERVIEW Condamine Valley Grain Co-operative is a registered export establishment located at 44 Cunningham Highway, Millmerran QLD 4357, QLD. The establishment holds RE Number RE-QLD-2022-0077 and is registered to handle and export Apples under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742. ## 2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE

EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY *Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted* | Item                                  | Quantity / Spec   | Purpose                     | |---------------------------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------| | Fruit washing and brushing line       | 1 unit            | Pre-grading hygiene         | | Optical grader (weight/colour/defect) | 1 unit            | Export grade sorting        | | Sticker/label applicator              | 1 unit            | Retail and export labelling | | Palletiser                            | 1 unit            | Export pallet build         | | Weigh-price labeller                  | 1 unit            | Consumer pack verification  | ## 4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES *Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3*

### 4.1  Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1) The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Apples. ### 4.2  Lighting (C2) LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 500 lux processing, 400 lux storage, 380 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements. ### 4.3  Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3) Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points. ## 5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS *Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6* ### 5.1  Cleanability (C4) Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots. ### 5.2  Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity. ### 5.3  Waste Disposal Design (C6) Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (1500 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed. ## 6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM *Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7* ### 6.1  Waste Management Procedures (C7) Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1001 Rev 3): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager. **Waste streams and handling arrangements:** | Waste Type                              | Handling Method                                     | Removal Frequency             | |-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|

| Fruit culls and trim waste              | Bins at grading line, hourly removal to compost bay | Daily                         | | Washdown water                          | Recessed drains → grease trap → trade waste         | Weekly grease trap inspection | | Packaging waste (film, cardboard, foam) | Baler in external waste bay                         | Fortnightly collection        | | Chemical containers                     | Sealed store, labelled                              | Quarterly licensed disposal   | ## 7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION *Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)* ### 7.1  Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8) All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated apples residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear. ### 7.2  Pest Condition (C9) No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation). ## 8. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs) *Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment* ### Receival / Intake Area Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log. ### Huller / Cracker / Sheller After each production run: Power off and lock out drive before opening. Dismantle outer access panels. Remove nut residue, shell fragments, and skin from rollers, screens, and internal surfaces using a stiff brush. Prepare BioDegreaser FD at 1:25. Apply to metal surfaces where oil residue is present. Contact time 5 minutes. Rinse with water. Allow to dry before reassembly. Record in Equipment Cleaning Log. ### Grading & Sizing Equipment After each run: Clear all nut product from grading screens and conveyor belts. Brush screens using designated nut-cleaning brush to remove embedded skins and fragments. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20 in a spray bottle. Spray conveyor belt and rollers.

Wipe with clean cloth. Inspect for any remaining organic residue. Record in Run Record. ### Drying Area / Pads / Dryer Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Drying Area / Pads / Dryer in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log. ### Storage Bins / Holding Area Between commodity lots: Inspect and clean storage bins before loading a new nut commodity. Using industrial vacuum, remove all residual nut material from bin walls, seams, and floor. Inspect for pest activity (insect frass, rodent droppings). Storage Manager signs pre-loading checklist confirming bin is clean and free of pests. ## 6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning. ## 7.
